                                 Opinion

  BRIGHT, J. The defendant, Jose T., appeals directly
to this court from his conviction of one count of sexual
assault in the first degree in violation of General Stat-
utes § 53a-70 (a) (2), one count of sexual assault in the
fourth degree in violation of General Statutes § 53a-73a
(a) (1) (A), and one count of risk of injury to a child in
violation of General Statutes § 53-21 (a) (2).1 His prin-
cipal claim on appeal is that the trial court improperly
instructed the jury that, to the extent the victim delayed
in reporting the alleged sexual abuse, “the mere fact of
that delay” should not be considered in evaluating her
credibility. The defendant contends that the instruction
was improper under State v. Daniel W. E., 322 Conn.
593, 629, 142 A.3d 265 (2016), and State v. Adam P.,
351 Conn. 213, 220, 226, 330 A.3d 73 (2025), which
subsequently overruled Daniel W. E., because delayed
disclosure was central to his theory that the victim had
fabricated the allegations and because he challenged the
victim’s credibility on that basis. The defendant further
contends that the challenged instruction violated his
constitutional right to present a closing argument. He
separately claims that the trial court erred in admitting
into evidence the video recording of the victim’s forensic
interview.
  We conclude that, because the defendant challenged
the victim’s credibility in part on the basis of her delayed
disclosure, it was improper under State v. Daniel W.
E., supra, 322 Conn. 629, for the trial court to give the
